title: Radio: UAS-11 Uncommanded Flight — Lake Risk

lines.text: Ops, I'm looking at the HMI. The aircraft is on a 150-meter eastward leg, now 110 meters north of the meadow. It will cross the north shore of the lake in 42 seconds. If it lands in the lake, recovery will require CCSO and the marine unit per ERP Section 4.3. The battery is at 82%. We cannot stop it in automation. We must switch to manual now.

fields.voiceStyle: Young adult female, steady, focused, urgent

instructorNote: This inject confirms the aircraft is on an uncommanded path toward the lake. The IC must decide whether to maintain automation or switch to manual control to attempt a controlled landing before it enters the water.

citations.documentTitle: Harwick UAS Operations Group — Emergency Response Plan for Flight Operations (ERP)
citations.quote: An aircraft in the lake or Millstone Creek is not recovered by the crew. The IC calls the site manager and CCSO; recovery uses the property's boat with life jackets or waits for the sheriff's marine

citations.documentTitle: Harwick UAS Operations Group — UAS Flight Operations & Safety Manual (FOM)
citations.headingPath: FOM › Section 9 › 9.3 GNSS degradation or spoofing suspicion
citations.quote: Signs: satellite count falls while the sky is clear; position jumps; RTK fix lost on both RTK-1 and the aircraft; the home point moves; DAA-1 and the GCS disagree on position. Actions: the RPIC switch
